# Pressure-Measuring Device with Optical Signal Transmission

## Overview

The present invention relates to a pressure-measuring device designed to convert mechanical or hydraulic pressurization into a measurable signal. This signal is subsequently forwarded to a remote evaluation unit, enabling the monitoring and analysis of pressure conditions from a distance. The device offers a reliable means of pressure detection suitable for a variety of industrial applications.

## Mounting and Installation

To ensure secure and stable operation, the pressure-measuring device is equipped with a fastening device. This fastening device serves to attach the pressure-measuring device directly to the machine housing of a motor or a pump. By securing the device in this manner, accurate and consistent pressure measurements can be obtained under operational conditions.

## Optical Signal Generation

At the core of the measuring functionality is a transmitter head located on the measuring device head. This transmitter head is connected to a light source by means of a first optical fiber. Through this connection, light is transmitted from the source to the transmitter head, which then emits the light across a defined light path. The use of optical fibers ensures efficient and interference-free transmission of the light signal.

## Signal Reception

Positioned directly opposite the transmitter head is a receiver head. The receiver head is arranged to receive the light emitted across the light path by the transmitter head. Once the light is received, it is conveyed to the evaluation unit by way of a second optical fiber. This arrangement allows the optical signal to be transferred to the evaluation unit for further processing and analysis.

## Measuring Principle

The operation of the device is based on the interaction between a measuring element and the light path. When mechanical or hydraulic pressure is applied, the measuring element moves into the light path situated between the transmitter head and the receiver head. This movement influences the light transmitted from the transmitter head to the receiver head, thereby generating a measurable variation in the optical signal that corresponds to the applied pressure. In this way, the device effectively translates physical pressurization into an optical measuring signal that can be interpreted by the remote evaluation unit.

# Optical Pressure-Measuring Device

## Overview

The present invention relates to a pressure-measuring device designed to convert mechanical or hydraulic pressurization into an optical measuring signal that can be transmitted to a remote evaluation unit. This approach offers significant advantages over conventional electrical pressure sensors, particularly in environments where electromagnetic interference, explosive atmospheres, or long-distance signal transmission present challenges to traditional measurement systems.

## System Components

The device comprises several interconnected components that work together to achieve accurate pressure measurement:

**Fastening Device:** A dedicated fastening mechanism secures the measuring apparatus to the system or vessel whose pressure is to be monitored. This ensures stable positioning and reliable coupling to the pressure source, whether mechanical or hydraulic in nature.

**Transmitter Head:** At the heart of the optical system, the transmitter head is connected to a light source by means of an optical fiber. The light source generates a consistent beam of light, which is guided through the fiber and emitted from the transmitter head into a defined light path.

**Receiver Head:** Positioned directly opposite the transmitter head, the receiver head captures the light that traverses the intervening light path. Any changes in the intensity or characteristics of the received light correspond directly to variations in the applied pressure.

**Displaceable Measuring Element:** A movable measuring element is arranged such that it can enter and exit the light path between the transmitter and receiver heads. This element is the key mechanical-to-optical converter within the system.

## Operating Principle

When mechanical or hydraulic pressure is applied to the device, the resulting force acts upon the displaceable measuring element, causing it to move into the light path established between the transmitter and receiver heads. As the measuring element advances into this path, it modulates the transmitted light—for example, by partially obscuring the beam or altering its intensity in proportion to the degree of displacement.

Because the extent of the measuring element's movement is directly related to the magnitude of the applied pressure, the corresponding modulation of the light signal provides an accurate optical representation of the pressure value. The receiver head detects this modulated light and generates a measuring signal accordingly.

## Signal Transmission and Evaluation

The optical measuring signal is subsequently forwarded to a remote evaluation unit, where it is processed and interpreted to determine the precise pressure reading. By relying on optical rather than purely electrical signal transmission, the device enables reliable remote monitoring over considerable distances while remaining immune to many of the disturbances that affect conventional electrical measurement systems.

## Advantages

This optical-based configuration delivers accurate and dependable pressure measurement, making it especially well-suited for demanding industrial applications. The separation of the sensing element from the electrical evaluation electronics enhances safety, reduces susceptibility to interference, and supports flexible integration into remote monitoring and control installations.

# The

The word "**the**" is the most frequently used word in the English language. Though small and often overlooked, it plays an essential role in how we communicate every single day.

## What Is "The"?

"The" is known as the **definite article**. Its job is to point to a specific noun that both the speaker and listener already know about. When you say "the dog," you are referring to a particular dog, not just any dog. This is what separates it from the indefinite articles "a" and "an," which refer to something general or unspecified.

## Why It Matters

Consider the difference between these two sentences:

- "Please hand me **a** book."
- "Please hand me **the** book."

In the first sentence, any book will do. In the second, you have a specific book in mind. This tiny word carries a surprising amount of meaning, guiding the listener toward exactly what you intend.

## A Word with History

The word "the" has ancient roots, evolving from Old English forms such as *se*, *seo*, and *þæt*. Over centuries, English speakers simplified these various forms into the single, versatile word we use today.

## Interesting Facts

- "The" appears in roughly **one out of every sixteen words** we read or write.
- Despite being so common, it is one of the trickiest words for English learners, since many languages do not use articles at all.
- It can be pronounced two ways: "thuh" before consonant sounds and "thee" before vowel sounds.

## Conclusion

Though it is only three letters long, "the" is a cornerstone of clear communication. It quietly shapes our sentences, adds precision to our meaning, and remains an indispensable part of the English language.

# Abstract

A pressure-measuring device for detecting pressure at a measurement location and transmitting corresponding measurement signals to a remotely located evaluation unit. The device comprises a pressure-sensitive sensor element configured to deform in response to an applied pressure, and at least one optical fiber optically coupled to the sensor element. Light propagating through the optical fiber is modulated as a function of the deformation of the sensor element, such that a characteristic of the transmitted light—for example, intensity, wavelength, phase, or polarization—varies in dependence on the measured pressure. The optical fiber transmits the modulated light signal over a distance to the remote evaluation unit, which is configured to receive the optical signal and to determine the pressure value therefrom. Because the measurement signal is transmitted optically, the device is substantially immune to electromagnetic interference and is suitable for use in hazardous, explosive, or high-voltage environments, as well as in applications requiring galvanic isolation between the measurement location and the evaluation unit. In a preferred embodiment, the sensor element comprises a membrane or diaphragm coupled to a fiber-optic component such as a Fabry-Pérot cavity or a fiber Bragg grating, enabling accurate and reliable pressure measurement over an extended transmission path.

# Patent Summary: Fiber-Optic Pressure Sensor for Motor/Pump Housing Mounting

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates to a fiber-optic pressure sensor (**100**) configured for mounting on a motor or pump housing to provide real-time pressure measurement in high-electromagnetic-interference (EMI) and harsh operating environments where conventional electrical sensors are prone to failure.

In accordance with one embodiment, the fiber-optic pressure sensor (**100**) comprises a sensor housing (**10**) having a mounting interface (**12**) adapted to be secured to an external surface of a motor or pump housing (**14**). The mounting interface (**12**) may include threaded portions (**16**) or a flange (**18**) enabling fluid-tight engagement with a pressure port (**20**) of the motor or pump housing (**14**).

A pressure-sensitive diaphragm (**22**) is disposed at a distal end of the sensor housing (**10**) and is arranged to deflect in response to fluid pressure (P) communicated through the pressure port (**20**). The diaphragm (**22**) may be formed of a corrosion-resistant material such as stainless steel or a silicon-based membrane.

An optical fiber (**30**) extends through the sensor housing (**10**) and terminates at a fiber end face (**32**) positioned in spaced-apart relation to the diaphragm (**22**), thereby defining a Fabry-Pérot optical cavity (**34**) therebetween. Deflection of the diaphragm (**22**) under applied pressure varies a cavity length (**L**) of the optical cavity (**34**), producing a corresponding modulation in an optical interference signal.

A ferrule (**36**) supports and aligns the optical fiber (**30**) within the sensor housing (**10**), maintaining optical alignment between the fiber end face (**32**) and the diaphragm (**22**). A hermetic seal (**38**) isolates the optical cavity (**34**) from ambient contaminants and process fluid.

The optical fiber (**30**) is optically coupled to a light source (**40**) and a photodetector (**42**) by way of an optical coupler (**44**). An interrogation and processing unit (**50**) receives the modulated optical signal from the photodetector (**42**) and computes a pressure value based on the detected variation in cavity length (**L**).

In a further embodiment, the sensor housing (**10**) incorporates a temperature-compensation element (**60**), such as a second reference fiber (**62**) or fiber Bragg grating (**64**), to correct for thermally induced measurement errors arising from motor or pump operation.

The sensor (**100**) is electrically passive at the point of measurement, rendering it immune to electromagnetic interference generated by motor windings and drive electronics, and is suitable for use in explosive, wet, or high-temperature environments.

counterfactuals.output:
# Optical Pressure Measurement Device

## Overview

This invention describes an apparatus for measuring mechanical or hydraulic pressure by converting physical displacement into an optically detectable signal. The system offers advantages including electrical isolation, immunity to electromagnetic interference, and suitability for hazardous environments.

## Core Components

**1. Light Source**
- Provides a stable illumination beam (typically an LED or laser diode)
- May emit visible or infrared light for reliable detection

**2. Transmitter Head**
- Houses and directs the light source
- Contains optics (lenses/collimators) to focus the beam into a defined light path
- Positioned to project light across a measurement gap

**3. Receiver Head**
- Positioned opposite the transmitter, aligned along the light path
- Contains a photodetector (photodiode or phototransistor)
- Converts received light intensity into an electrical signal

**4. Displaceable Measuring Element**
- A movable member (shutter, vane, or aperture plate) coupled to a pressure-sensing component
- Positioned within the light path between transmitter and receiver
- Moves proportionally to applied pressure

## Operating Principle

```
[Pressure Input]
       ↓
[Pressure-sensing element: diaphragm/piston/bellows]
       ↓
[Displaceable measuring element moves]
       ↓
Light Source → Transmitter → [Interrupted Beam] → Receiver → Signal
```

1. **Pressure Application:** Mechanical or hydraulic pressure acts on a sensing element (e.g., a diaphragm, piston, or Bourdon tube).

2. **Displacement:** The pressure causes proportional movement of the displaceable measuring element (shutter/vane).

3. **Light Interruption:** As the element moves into the light path, it progressively **blocks or attenuates** the beam traveling from transmitter to receiver.

4. **Detection:** The receiver measures the resulting change in light intensity. A greater pressure produces greater displacement, causing more interruption and reduced received light.

5. **Signal Output:** The photodetector output is calibrated so light intensity corresponds directly to pressure magnitude.

## Design Variations

- **Graduated shutter:** A wedge-shaped or slotted vane produces analog, continuous readings
- **Multiple beam paths:** Several light paths enable digital/incremental resolution
- **Reflective configuration:** Transmitter and receiver on the same side, with the measuring element acting as a moving reflector

## Advantages

- No electrical contacts at the measurement point (intrinsically safe)
- High sensitivity and fast response
- Resistant to corrosion and electromagnetic interference
- Contactless sensing reduces mechanical wear

---

# Summary of the Invention

## Overview

The present invention relates to an optical pressure gauge configured for reliable pressure measurement in environments where electrical sensing may be disadvantageous or hazardous. The invention overcomes limitations of conventional pressure gauges by employing an optical sensing arrangement in combination with a dedicated fastening device that enables secure and repeatable installation.

## Principal Aspects

In accordance with a first aspect of the invention, there is provided an optical pressure gauge comprising a transmitter head and a receiver head, the transmitter head and the receiver head being optically coupled to a sensing element responsive to applied pressure. The transmitter head is configured to emit optical radiation, and the receiver head is configured to detect optical radiation modulated in response to a pressure-induced change at the sensing element.

In accordance with a further aspect, the transmitter head and the receiver head are connected to a remote signal processing unit by way of one or more optical fibers. This arrangement permits the electrically passive sensing portion of the gauge to be located at the point of measurement, while active optoelectronic components may be positioned at a safe or convenient distance therefrom. As a result, the gauge is well suited for use in explosive atmospheres, high-voltage environments, and areas subject to strong electromagnetic interference.

In accordance with a still further aspect, the optical pressure gauge includes a fastening device configured to mechanically secure the gauge to a structure, conduit, vessel, or measurement port. The fastening device provides mechanical stability and maintains alignment between the sensing element and the optical heads, thereby improving measurement accuracy and repeatability.

## Advantages

Embodiments of the invention may provide one or more of the following advantages:

- **Intrinsic safety**, owing to the absence of electrical potential at the point of measurement;
- **Immunity to electromagnetic interference**, resulting from the use of optical rather than electrical signal transmission;
- **Remote measurement capability**, permitting the signal processing unit to be located away from the sensing location by means of the optical fibers;
- **Secure and repeatable mounting**, provided by the fastening device, which maintains optical alignment under mechanical and thermal loading;
- **Simplified installation and maintenance**, resulting from the modular arrangement of the transmitter head, receiver head, and fastening device.

## Preferred Features

In certain embodiments, the transmitter head and the receiver head are integrated within a common housing that is engageable with the fastening device. In other embodiments, the transmitter head and the receiver head are disposed in a spaced-apart, opposed relationship such that optical radiation traverses the sensing element therebetween.

The sensing element may comprise a deflectable diaphragm, an optically transmissive membrane, or an interferometric or intensity-modulating structure whose optical response varies as a function of applied pressure. The one or more optical fibers may comprise single-mode or multimode fibers, and may include separate transmit and receive fibers or a shared bidirectional optical path.

The fastening device may comprise a threaded coupling, a clamp, a flange, a bayonet fitting, or an equivalent mechanical interface adapted to the intended installation. In preferred embodiments, the fastening device incorporates a sealing arrangement to isolate the sensing element from an external environment while exposing it to a pressure to be measured.

## General Statement

The foregoing summary is provided to introduce a selection of concepts in a simplified form. It is not intended to identify essential features of the claimed subject matter, nor is it intended to limit the scope of the claims. Additional features, aspects, and advantages of the invention will become apparent from the detailed description, the accompanying drawings, and the appended claims.

# Pressure-Measuring Apparatus Utilizing Optical Fiber Signal Conversion

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to an apparatus for measuring pressure, and more particularly to a pressure-measuring apparatus that converts a pressurization applied thereto into an optically transmissible measuring signal by means of optical fibers cooperating with a movable measuring element disposed within a light path.

## Summary of the Apparatus

In accordance with the present invention, there is provided a pressure-measuring apparatus comprising a housing having a pressure-receiving region adapted to be exposed to a medium whose pressure is to be determined. A movable measuring element is disposed within said housing and is arranged for displacement along a predetermined path in response to a pressurization acting thereon.

The apparatus further comprises a light-transmitting optical fiber arrangement including at least a first optical fiber constituting a light-supplying conductor and a second optical fiber constituting a light-receiving conductor, said first and second optical fibers being optically coupled across a light path within which said movable measuring element is at least partially positioned.

## Detailed Description of the Operative Principle

**Light Emission and Reception.** Light emanating from a light source is coupled into the proximal end of said first optical fiber and is conducted therethrough to a distal end thereof, whereupon said light is emitted into said light path. Said second optical fiber is positioned to receive, at a distal end thereof, at least a portion of the light traversing said light path, and to conduct said received portion to a photoelectric transducer means operative to convert the received light intensity into a corresponding electrical measuring signal.

**Modulation by the Measuring Element.** Said movable measuring element is operatively coupled to said pressure-receiving region such that a pressurization applied to said region effects a displacement of said measuring element relative to said light path. Said displacement causes said measuring element to variably intercept, attenuate, deflect, or otherwise modulate the quantity of light passing from said first optical fiber to said second optical fiber.

Accordingly, the intensity of light received by said second optical fiber varies as a monotonic function of the position of said measuring element, which position is in turn a function of the applied pressure. In this manner, the applied pressurization is converted into a corresponding variation in received light intensity.

**Signal Derivation.** Said photoelectric transducer means generates an electrical output signal representative of the received light intensity, whereby said output signal constitutes a measure of the pressurization applied to said pressure-receiving region. Evaluation means may be connected to said transducer means for deriving therefrom a pressure value in accordance with a predetermined calibration relationship.

## Illustrative Embodiments

In one embodiment, said measuring element comprises a shutter or diaphragm-actuated vane movable transversely across said light path, whereby increasing pressure progressively occludes said light path to reduce the received light intensity.

In an alternative embodiment, said measuring element comprises a reflective surface displaceable relative to the distal ends of said first and second optical fibers, whereby the proportion of light reflected from said first optical fiber into said second optical fiber varies in dependence upon the position of said reflective surface.

In a further embodiment, said pressure-receiving region comprises a resilient diaphragm mechanically coupled to said measuring element, said diaphragm deflecting in response to pressure and thereby imparting a corresponding displacement to said measuring element.

## Advantages

The apparatus affords the advantage of immunity to electromagnetic interference within the pressure-sensing region, by reason of the optical—rather than electrical—transmission of the measuring signal along said optical fibers, and further permits the electrical transducer and evaluation means to be located remotely from the pressure-receiving region.

---
